Here is what the Before You Call: Quick Checks document (faq/troubleshooting_before_you_call.md) says for the main situations.

If your AC isn't cooling or is blowing warm air, confirm the thermostat is set to COOL with the set point below room temperature, and check the air filter, since a clogged filter is the #1 cause of weak airflow.
Check the breaker panel and reset any tripped breaker once; if it trips again, stop.
Check the outdoor unit for debris or a fan that isn't spinning.
If the indoor coil is iced over, turn the system OFF with the fan ON for 2 hours to thaw before the technician arrives.
If water is pooling at the indoor unit, turn the system off to prevent overflow damage, and don't pour bleach into the line unless a technician instructs you to.

If the thermostat screen is blank, replace the batteries if it has them, check the breaker for the air handler, and check the float switch in the condensate pan, since a full drain pan can cut power to the thermostat on many systems.

Separately, the Warranty Policy (warranty/warranty_policy.md, Filing a claim) says that if a failure is covered there is no diagnostic fee, but if the technician determines it is not covered, the standard $89 diagnostic fee applies.
